column1: # shellcheck_legacy_exceptions.tsv -- TEMPLATE (gate DATA format). A consumer keeps exactly ONE copy at the
# canonical path config/shellcheck_legacy_exceptions.tsv; a bound run uses that file automatically (read from
# the REVIEWED HEAD) and refuses any other --shellcheck-exceptions path. Review every change to it like code.
# Parsed by review/lib/precheck_pack_run.py _parse_exceptions. One row per file, 5 TAB-separated fields:
#   path  reason_class  tracked_item  pinned_counts  pin_date
# path: normalised repo-relative path (no "..", no leading "/", no backslash) of a file TRACKED AT THE BATCH
#   BASE -- a script new in the batch cannot exempt itself.
# reason_class (closed set), each checked against evidence in the reviewed file:
#   too-large-to-lint-in-budget  the file has >= 5000 lines
#   generated                    a generated-file marker ("generated by", "do not edit", "auto-generated") in its first 20 lines
#   vendored                     a vendored path component (vendor/, third_party/, external/, ...)
# tracked_item: the tracked work item that removes the exception (e.g. ATM-1234)
# pinned_counts: per-rule counts of BLOCKING findings at pin time, e.g. SC2086=12,SC2034=3,DIR-UNJUSTIFIED=1
#   (- for none). Blocking = error/warning level plus info SC2086 SC2030 SC2031 SC2162 SC2059; other
#   findings are advisory and never counted. SC10xx (parse) codes cannot be pinned: a parse error in a
#   listed file always FAILs. A count above its pin, or a rule absent from the pin, FAILs; lower counts PASS
#   (lower the pin in a reviewed change).
# New rows and raised pins: compared with the BASE commit's copy of this file. Accepted only in a batch that
#   changes nothing but this file (and listed for the reviewer); in any other batch they FAIL.
# A listed file is still subject to the hard caps (8 GiB memory, 10,000 lines / 2 MiB): an exception cannot
#   make an over-cap file reviewable -- split it first.
# pin_date: YYYY-MM-DD
# Residual: a finding swapped for another of the SAME rule is invisible to per-rule counts.
